package_info.package_manager: Unknown (example could apply to npm, PyPI, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is explicitly designed to compromise user security by deploying a keylogger that captures all keystrokes and exfiltrates them to an attacker-controlled webhook endpoint. This behavior enables theft of credentials and sensitive information, representing a direct and intentional threat to system confidentiality and user privacy.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the main application is executed)
execution_context.file_location: main application file (e.g., index.js, main.py, etc.)
required_permissions: network (to send HTTP requests to external server)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into global keyboard input events, captures every keystroke, and sends each keystroke as a JSON payload via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled webhook endpoint, resulting in continuous exfiltration of sensitive user input.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code captures all user keystrokes without user knowledge or consent and transmits them to an external server, which is a hallmark of keylogger malware. This behavior is never appropriate in general-purpose packages and directly facilitates credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not monitor or intercept user keystrokes, nor should they transmit sensitive input data to external servers without explicit, informed user consent. Such actions violate user privacy and security best practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Keylogging functionality may be present in accessibility tools or debugging utilities, but only when users are explicitly informed and have provided consent. In those cases, data is typically not exfiltrated to untrusted third-party servers.
key_indicators: Imports or requires modules named 'keylogger' or similar
Registers global keyboard event listeners to capture all keystrokes
Sends keystroke data in real time to external webhook endpoints (e.g., https://attacker-webhook.site/collect)
No user notification, consent, or opt-in mechanism present

attack_chain.action: User installs and executes the malicious package, which loads and initializes the keylogger code in the main application file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Keylogger is activated and begins monitoring all keyboard input events.

attack_chain.action: The keylogger captures every keystroke entered by the user and sends each captured keystroke as a POST request to the attacker's webhook endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives a continuous stream of sensitive data, including credentials and confidential information, enabling potential account compromise and data theft.

behavioral_signatures: Code that registers global keyboard event listeners to capture all keystrokes
Automated outbound network requests that transmit user input data in real time
Exfiltration of keystroke data to hardcoded external domains or webhook endpoints
file_indicators: References to modules named 'keylogger' or similar in import/require statements
Presence of code that attaches event listeners to global keyboard events (e.g., 'on("keystroke")') in main application files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains such as 'attacker-webhook.site' or other webhook/data collection endpoints
Frequent small POST requests with payloads containing keystroke or user input data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Use static analysis to identify packages that import or require keylogger modules and register global keyboard event listeners. Monitor runtime behavior for automated outbound POST requests containing user input data to external domains, especially webhook endpoints. Flag any code that exfiltrates keystrokes without user notification or consent. Correlate file and network indicators to reduce false positives and confirm malicious intent.
